Dans cette leçon, vous découvrirez variables, constantes et types de données. Mais avant cela, vous devez connaître quelques notions de base sur la manière dont les données sont stockées dans la mémoire de l'ordinateur.

Une mémoire d'ordinateur (RAM) consiste en une séquence d'emplacements de mémoire pour stocker des programmes et des données. Chaque emplacement dispose d'un adresse numérique unique qui commence à 0. Vous pouvez considérer la mémoire comme une commode où chaque tiroir représente un emplacement mémoire. Supposons maintenant que vous donniez un numéro unique à chaque tiroir pour indiquer son emplacement ; le premier tireur reçoit le numéro 0, le second le 1, et ainsi de suite. Une adresse mémoire dans ce cas serait le numéro que vous attribuez à chaque tiroir.

Pourquoi avons-nous besoin de mémoire informatique ? Comme indiqué ci-dessus, la mémoire de l'ordinateur stocke les programmes et les données. Lorsque vous démarrez un programme, le programme est d'abord chargé dans la mémoire avant son exécution. Cela améliore les performances d'exécution. Après le démarrage de l'exécution, le programme peut sauvegarder et restaurer les données de la mémoire.

Comment tout cela est-il lié aux variables ? Le programme doit identifier où les données sont stockées dans la mémoire. Cela peut être fait en utilisant des adresses mémoire. Un moyen plus simple consiste à étiqueter ces emplacements de mémoire et à utiliser ces étiquettes lors de l'accès aux données. Pensez à étiqueter les emplacements de mémoire comme mettre un autocollant sur un tiroir avec un nom, comme dans l'exemple ci-dessous. Lorsque vous faites référence à ce tiroir, vous pouvez dire tiroir #3 ou tiroir Adam . Une variable est un nom que vous donnez à un emplacement mémoire dans votre programme.

Remarque : dans certains cas, un compilateur d'optimisation peut stocker une variable dans une mémoire spéciale appelée registre. Cependant, cela dépasse le cadre de cette introduction leçon.

e introduction leçon.

In this lesson, you will learn about variables, constants, and data types. But before we do that, you need to know a few basics about how data is stored in the computer's memory.

A computer's memory (RAM) consists of a sequence of memory locations for storing programs and data. Each location has a unique numeric address which starts from 0. You can think of memory as a chest of drawers where each drawer represents one memory location. Now assume you give a unique number to each drawer to indicate its location; the first drawer gets the number 0, the second gets 1, and so on. A memory address in this case would be the number you give to each drawer.

Why do we need computer memory? As indicated above, computer memory stores programs and data. When you start a program, the program is first loaded into the memory before it is executed. This improves the execution performance. After execution starts, the program can save and restore data from the memory.

How is this all related to variables? The program needs to identify where the data is stored in the memory. This can be done using memory addresses. An easier way is to label those memory locations and using these labels when accessing data. Think of labeling memory locations as putting a sticker on a drawer with a name, as in the example below. When referring to that drawer, you can either say drawer #3 or Adam's drawer. A variable is a name you give to a memory location in your program.

Note: in some cases, an optimizing compiler may store a variable in a special memory called a register. However, this is beyond the scope of this introductory lesson.

Declaring and Initializing Variables

Declaring a variable means informing the compiler that this variable will be used in the program. Initializing a variable means to store data in a variable for the first time. We use the assignment operator = to store data in variables. The general syntax is:

datatype variable_name = initial_value;

In Java, you must specify a type when declaring a variable, e.g. use int for integers. This allows the compiler to do type checking. Java is, therefore, classified as a statically-typed language. In the example below, the keyword int indicates that the variable is of integer type, which means it can only store integers (whole numbers).

In Python, you do not specify a type when declaring a variable. The compiler will infer the type based on the value assigned in the variable. The print() Function

This function prints data we put inside () to the screen (by default). The data could be one of the following:

  • A single item, e.g., string or number. For example, print("abc") displays abc on the screen.
  • An expression of which result is printed. For example, print(4 + 2) displays 6.

You can send multiple items separated by commas , to this function. For example, print("I have", 3, "books") displays I have 3 books.

The print function, by default, will move the cursor to the next line after it prints the data.

Customizing print Function

To change the default behaviour of the print function, you can use this general syntax:

print(data, sep=, end=, file=file, flush=flush)
  • sep: changes the default separator. Example: print("I have", 3, "books", sep='*') prints I have*3*books.
  • end: changes the default behavior of moving to a new line. Example: print("Hi", end="") does not move the cursor to the next line.

Introduction

When writing a program, you can decide which statements to execute based on certain conditions.

For example, informing users whether they are adults based on their age. The algorithm could be something like this:

Read user's age.
IF age is at least 18, THEN display "Adult".

In the above algorithm, displaying the message is controlled by the condition. Only if the condition is true will the word Adult be displayed.

You can use any of the following mechanisms to implement decision making in your program:

Context

Order of operations matters, they say! During one of the evenings, you were watching memes on Reddit. You spotted a picture of how different calculators evaluate math equations. You asked yourself, can I write my own calculator software? You decided to try! Because you are smart, you attempted to code a calculator which can handle multiple math operations.

Task

Write the program that:

  • Asks the user to input the math equation with exactly two operations as a string, e.g. "3+4*5".
  • Parse the equation and determine the order of operations. Remembere that *, / always come before +,- when evaluating equation.
  • Calculate and display the result.

Assumptions:

To simplify the problem, assume that the equation string will

  • only include single-digit, positive integers and two of the four operators +, -, *, and /.
  • not have negative numbers, floating-point numbers, other operators, spaces, or brackets.
  • always be valid in the form d$d$d where d is a digit and $ is an operator.

That means the input string will always have 5 characters (3 digits and 2 operators).

That is, your program should be able to handle all these equations:

  • "4+2*3"
  • "4/2-3"

However, your program should not handle any of these:

  • "-4*2+3", negatives are not allowed
  • "4 + 2 + 3", spaces are not allowed.
  • "4*(2+3)", brackets are not allowed.
  • "4*2.2+3", floating-point numbers are not allowed.

Switch Statement in Python

In Python, a match statement is used to choose one of several code blocks to execute.

match expression:
case value1:
//code block 1 is executed if expression == value1
case value2:
//code block 2 is executed if expression == value2
...
 case _:
//default code is executed if expression does not match any value

The value of the expression is computed once. Then, this value is compared with the value of each case. The case that matches the expression is executed. Unlike Java, there is no need of a break statement for the program to exit the match block; after the appropriate code block is executed, we automatically exit the match block.

If no match is found, the case _ case is executed.

    Types of Loop Condition

    The example you saw on the previous page uses a counter to keep track of the number of repetitions (aka iterations) and control when the loop stops. This type of loops is called counter-controlled repetition. We also have another type called sentinel-controlled repetition. Next, we discuss these two types when used in a while loop.

    Types de condition de boucle

    L'exemple que vous avez vu sur la page précédente utilise un compteur pour suivre le nombre de répétitions (ou itérations) et contrôler le moment où la boucle s'arrête. Ce type de boucles est appelé répétition contre-contrôlée. Nous avons aussi un autre type appelé répétition contrôlée par des sentinelles. Ensuite nous discuter de ces deux types lorsqu'ils sont utilisés dans un while boucle.

    a) Boucles contre-contrôlées

    Ici, nous utilisons une variable compteur pour contrôler la répétition. La syntaxe générale comporte trois composants :

The range() function creates a sequence of numbers that, by default, starts from 0, is incremented by 1, and stops before a specified value. For example, range(3) returns 0, 1, 2. This default behaviour can be changed as follows:

range (n) returns [0, 1, 2, ... , n-1]


range (n, m)returns [n, n+1, n+2, ... , m-2, m-1]
range (n, m, step)returns [n, n+step, n+2step, n+3step, ...]

For example,

  • range(5) creates the sequence [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] (note that 5 is not included)

La fonction range()

Nous pouvons utiliser la range() fonction pour générer une séquence pour le for lorsqu'elle est utilisée pour simplifier une boucle while.

La fonction range() crée une séquence de nombres qui, par défaut, part de 0, est incrémenté de 1, et s'arrête avant une valeur spécifiée. Par exemple, range(3) renvoie 0, 1, 2. Cette valeur par défaut le comportement peut être modifié comme suit :

for counter in range(start, end, step):
# loop body

where

  • start is the first value the counter is initialized to. This value is optional (see the range function).
  • end - 1 is the last value the counter takes for running the loop body.
  • step is the counter increment value for each new iteration. This value is optional (see the range function).

  • étape est l'étape valeur d'incrément du compteur pour chaque nouvelle itération. Cette valeur est facultative (voir la fonction de plage).

Floating Point Accuracy

As you may know, computers use binary format (0's and 1's) to represent data. This of course includes numeric data. This representation works well for whole numbers. However, it sometimes fails to accurately represent fractions. For example, the following code is expected to print 1.2 in both statements, right? However, the actual output of the second statement is 1.2000000000000002.

Where does this inaccuracy come from? This brings us back to the way computers represent data in binary (0 and 1). Many decimal fractions are approximated when stored in computers. The value 0.1 is represented in binary using a very long sequence 0.000110011001100110... which must be approximated in order to store it in computer memory.

A nice analogy is when you (human) want to write the fraction 2/3 as a decimal number. You will have to write 0.66666666666.. which is infinitely long, and you

ted in binary using a very long sequence 0.000110011001100110... which must be approximated in order to store it in computer memory.

A nice analogy is when you (human) want to write the fraction 2/3 as a decimal number. You will have to write 0.66666666666.. which is infinitely long, and you can only approximate it to something like 0.66667. The computer does the same thing with decimal fractions.

Why is this important to know here? As seen in the code above, the result of 1.1 + 0.1 is not equal to 1.2. Knowing that now, you should NOT use floating-point values with equality checking in loop condition.

D'où vient cette inexactitude ? Cela nous ramène à la façon dont les ordinateurs représentent les données en binaire (0 et 1). De nombreuses fractions décimales sont approximée lorsqu'elle est stockée dans des ordinateurs. La valeur 0.1 est représentée en binaire en utilisant une très longue séquence 0.000110011001100110... qui doit être approchée pour stockez-le dans la mémoire de l'ordinateur.

Une belle analogie est lorsque vous (humain) voulez écrire la fraction 2/3 sous forme de nombre décimal. Vous devrez écrire 0.66666666666.. qui est infiniment long, et vous ne pouvez l'approcher que de quelque chose comme 0,66667. L'ordinateur fait le même chose avec les fractions décimales.

Pourquoi est-ce important de savoir ici ? Comme on le voit dans le code ci-dessus, le résultat de 1,1 + 0,1 n'est pas égal à 1,2. Sachant cela maintenant, vous ne devriez PAS utiliser valeurs à virgule flottante avec vérification d'égalité en condition de boucle.

Qu'est-ce que la structure des données

Une structure de données est une collection d'éléments de données stockés dans la mémoire afin que ils peuvent être utilisés efficacement. Il existe plusieurs types de structures de données, toutes conçu pour organiser les données d'une manière qui sert un objectif spécifique. Exemples de types des structures de données comprennent des tableaux, des listes, des arbres, des tas, etc., chacun avec ses propres manière de stocker et de récupérer des données. Différentes applications et tâches ont différents besoins et limitations, et donc il faut utiliser la structure de données type qui correspond le mieux à ces besoins.

What is Data Structure

A data structure is a collection of data items stored in the memory so that they can be used effectively. There are several types of data structures, all designed to arrange data in a way that serves a specific purpose. Example types of data structures include arrays, lists, trees, heaps, etc, each with its own way of storing and retrieving data. Different applications and tasks have different needs and limitations, and hence one should use the data structure type that best fits these needs.

Array Basics

What is an Array?

An array is a collection of data items of the same type stored under one variable. For example, we can create an array called grades to store the grades of 100 students. All these values will be stored under a single name grades (as opposed to creating 100 separate variables to store them).

Array Basics

What is an Array?

An array is a collection of data items of the same type stored under one variable. For example, we can create an array called grades to store the grades of 100 students. All these values will be stored under a single name grades (as opposed to creating 100 separate variables to store them).

In Python, you can implement arrays either using lists or arrays module. A key difference is, lists allow to store items of different datatypes while arrays module does not allow that. This lesson discusses the use of Python lists to implement arrays as defined in other languages. More on Python lists will be discussed in the next lesson.

Principes de Arrays

Qu'est-ce qu'un tableau ?

Un tableau est une collection d'éléments de données du même type stockés sous un même variable. Par exemple, nous pouvons créez un tableau appelé grades pour stocker les classes de 100 élèves. Toutes ces valeurs seront stockés sous un seul nom notes (au lieu de créer 100 notes distinctes variables pour les stocker).

En Python, vous pouvez implémenter des tableaux en utilisant des listesou tableaux module. Création sans initialisation

Vous pouvez créer un tableau sans l'initialiser en utilisant cette syntaxe :

arrayName = []

La déclaration ci-dessus crée un tableau vide. Vous pouvez ajouter des valeurs à ce tableau ultérieurement.

Creating without Initialization

You can create an array without initializing it using this syntax:

arrayName = []

Above statement creates an empty array. You can add values to that array later.

Creating without Initialization

You can create an array without initializing it using this syntax:

datatype[] arrayName = new datatype[arraySize]

where the arraySize is the number of elements in the array. The array will be assigned default values as follows:

  • 0 for numeric primitive types (e.g. int, double, etc)
  • \u0000 for char types
  • false for boolean types
  • null for object types (such as String)

Example

// nums contains {0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
int[] nums = new int[5];

//flag contains {false, false, false}
boolean flag = new boolean[3];

You can also create the array over two lines as in the example below.

Example

// nums contains {0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
int[] nums;
nums = new int[5];

3) Utilisation de System.arraycopy()

System.arraycopy() est une méthode intégrée qui permet de copier des éléments de tableau. La syntaxe est :

System.arraycopy(src, srcPos, dest, destPos, length)

Où :

  • src est le tableau source
  • srcPos est le début place dans la source array
  • dest le tableau de destination
  • destPos est le position de départ dans la destination data
  • length est le nombre d'éléments de tableau à copier.

Pour utiliser cette méthode pour cloner un tableau existant, vous devez d'abord créer un tableau vide de même taille que celui existant. Ensuite, utilisez System.arraycopy(src, 0, dest, 0, src.length) pour copier tous les éléments d'un tableau source src au tableau de destination dest.

    Bases de la liste

    Comme mentionné dans les leçons précédentes, il est courant de travailler avec des collections de données lors du développement d'un programme.

    La bibliothèque standard C++ inclut plusieurs structures de données utilisées pour gérer les données. Cette leçon se concentre sur les vecteurs.

    Les vecteurs sont des structures de données dynamiques et polyvalentes qui fournissent de nombreuses opérations pour effectuer sur vos collectes de données. Certaines des caractéristiques clés des vecteurs sont :

    • Redimensionnable : ; Les vecteurs peuvent se développer au besoin lorsque vous ajoutez plus d'articles.
    • Commandé : chaque article a son propre index qui indique son commande dans la liste.
    • Autoriser les doublons : vous pouvez avoir deux articles ou plus avec la même valeur stockée dans le vecteur.
    • Ne pas autoriser différents types de données : les vecteurs ne peuvent pas stocker éléments de différents types, mais il existe d'autres bibliothèques de support que vous pouvez utiliser pour contourner.

    Dans cette leçon, nous aborderons les opérations couramment utilisées que vous pouvez effectuer sur les vecteurs, à savoir comment :

    • Créer des vecteurs.
    • Accéder, ajouter, supprimer et modifier des éléments vectoriels
    • Vecteurs en boucle
    • Trier et inverser les vecteurs
    • Copier et fusionner des vecteurs

What is a Function?

A function is a named block of reusable code that performs a specific task. Whenever you want to perform this task, you need to call (invoke) the function by its name. A function runs only when its name is called.

A function may optionally receive input data (called arguments) and return a value. We will discuss this shortly.


Qu'est-ce qu'une fonction ?

Une fonction est un bloc nommé de code réutilisable qui exécute une tâche spécifique. Chaque fois que vous souhaitez effectuer cette tâche, vous devez appeler (invoquer) la fonction par son nom. Une fonction s'exécute uniquement lorsque son nom est appelé.

Une fonction peut éventuellement recevoir des données d'entrée (appelées arguments) et retourner une valeur. Nous en discuterons sous peu.

What is a Method?

A method is a named block of reusable code that performs a specific task. Whenever you want to perform this task, you need to call (invoke) the method by its name. A method runs only when its name is called.

A method may optionally receive input data (called arguments) and return a value. We will discuss this shortly.

What is a Method?

What actually happens when you call a function?

When calling a function, the flow of control shifts from the calling statement to the called function. After the function is completed, the control is shifted back to the calling statement.

Lors de l'appel d'une fonction, le flux de contrôle passe de l'appelant instruction à la fonction appelée. Une fois la fonction terminée, la commande est ramené à l'instruction d'appel.

What actually happens when you call a method?

When calling a method, the flow of control shifts from the calling statement to the called method. After the method is completed, the control is shifted back to the calling statement.

What actually happens when you call a method?

When calling a method, the flow of control shifts from the calling statement to the called method. After the method is completed, the control is shifted back to the calling statement.

Introduction

When writing a program, you can decide which statements to execute based on certain conditions.

For example, informing users whether they are adults based on their age. The algorithm could be something like this:

Read user's age.
IF age is at least 18, THEN display "Adult".

In the above algorithm, displaying the message is controlled by the condition. Only if the condition is true will the word Adult be displayed.

You can use any of the following mechanisms to implement decision making in your program:

Like an if statement, the code inside the while loop will only run if the condition is true. However, after executing the code, the condition is checked again; if it is still true, the loop body is executed again, and so on. If the condition is false, the program continues to the next code block right after the loop body.

Précision de l'Floating Point

Comme vous le savez peut-être, les ordinateurs utilisent le format binaire (0 et 1) pour représenter les données. Cela inclut bien sûr les données numériques. Cette représentation fonctionne bien pour les nombres entiers. Cependant, il échoue parfois à représenter avec précision les fractions. Par exemple, le code suivant devrait imprimer 1.2 dans les deux instructions, n'est-ce pas ? Cependant, la sortie réelle de la deuxième instruction est 1,2000000000000002.

Floating Point Accuracy

As you may know, computers use binary format (0's and 1's) to represent data. This of course includes numeric data. This representation works well for whole numbers. However, it sometimes fails to accurately represent fractions. For example, the following code is expected to print 1.2 in both statements, right? However, the actual output of the second statement is 1.2000000000000002.

Java English Computer Science text Programming_Languages System.out.println(1.2); //output: 1.2 System.out.println(1.1 + 0.1); //output: 1.2000000000000002 print(1.2) # output: 1.2 print(1.1 + 0.1) # output: 1.2000000000000002 Java English Computer Science code Spoken_Languages

Where does this inaccuracy come from? This brings us back to the way computers represent data in binary (0 and 1). Many decimal fractions are approximated when stored in computers. The value 0.1 is represented in binary using a very long sequence 0.000110011001100110... which must be approximated in order to store it in computer memory.

A nice analogy is when you (human) want to write the fraction 2/3 as a decimal number. You will have to write 0.66666666666.. which is infinitely long, and you can only approximate it to something like 0.66667. The computer does the same thing with decimal fractions.

Why is this important to know here? As seen in the code above, the result of 1.1 + 0.1 is not equal to 1.2. Knowing that now, you should NOT use floating-point values with equality checking in loop condition.

Context

You are given data that is recorded as a rocket started its descent into the Earth's atmosphere and landed in the Atlantic Ocean. The data is stored as an array of integers which represent the altitude of the rocket in meters. Negative values represent the altitude below sea level. Zero altitudes belong to the "Above Ocean" group.

Task

Create a function named getData that receives two arguments:

  • An array of integers, named altitudes, representing the rocket's altitude.
  • A string, named type, that may have one of three values: "above", "below", or "minmax".

The function should return an array with values copied from the altitudes array. The returned values will depend on the type argument.

  • If type is "above", return an array containing all altitudes above the ocean.
  • If type is "below", return altitudes below the ocean.
  • If type is minmax, then return an array containing two elements: [lowest altitude, highest altitude]. Note that the lowest value comes first.

This process continues until the base case is reached, at which point the function returns a value. The recursive calls build upon each other, gradually solving larger instances of the problem until the original problem is solved.

La récursivité est une technique puissante pour résoudre des problèmes compliqués en les décomposant en problèmes plus petits et plus gérables. La récursivité implique qu'une fonction s'appelle elle-même dans sa propre définition. En fait, une telle fonction est appelée une fonction récursive.

En récursivité, une fonction résout un cas de base (généralement, la version la plus simple du problème) directement, puis s'appelle avec une entrée modifiée pour résoudre une version plus petite du problème original. Ce processus continue jusqu'à ce que le cas de base soit atteint, moment auquel la fonction retourne une valeur. Les appels récursifs se construisent les uns sur les autres, résolvant progressivement des instances plus grandes du problème jusqu'à ce que le problème original soit résolu.

Thinking Recursively

In this lesson, we will walkthrough the process of thinking recursively on a problem.

Looking at the last example of the print function, one might wonder why we even need recursion when we can use loops. In fact, any recursive code can be rewritten as iterative code using loops (and the opposite is also true!). However, recursion might simplify some problems significantly. Solving some problems with iteration might be much more challenging and require more code, but will be much more efficient. So, both approaches have their place, but knowing how to think recursively is very helpful!

Thinking recursively involves three crucial steps:

  1. Identify the recursive call (i.e. the simpler form)
  2. Identify stopping condition(s) by identifying base case(s)
  3. Write the recursive method

Can we reduce the problem to a smaller one? Note that to reach the end position, we must either reach the position above the end position or the position left of the end position. Thus, we can say that the number of different paths reaching the "end" is equal to the sum of the number of ways to reach positions above it and to its left.

Let f(m,n) be the number of paths from start to end. Thus, by the above discussion:

f(m, n) = f(m, n-1) + f(m-1, n)

This gives us an idea of how the recursive calls are going to work -- we simply return f(m, n-1) + f(m-1, n). But, what should be our stopping condition (also known as the Base case)? Well, at each step, the size of grid is getting smaller (this is the essence of recursive problem solving; smaller problems build up to solve bigger ones!) and thus, we will reach a point when we just need the number of paths in a m x 1 or 1 x n grid. Obviously, in both these case, the answer is going to be 1 because there is only one route: going either only right or only down, respectively. Thus, we have

f(m, 1) = f(1, n) = 1

and this could be our base case. We now have our solution in theory! Writing the code is the easy part:

More On Recursion

While recursive methods are intuitive and easy to implement, they can sometimes have performance issues due to excessive stack usage and slower execution. One technique to mitigate these issues is tail recursion.

Tail Recursion

Tail recursion is a special type of recursion where the recursive call is the last operation performed in the function, i.e., there are no pending operations or computations after the recursive call. This allows the compiler or interpreter to optimize the recursion by reusing the current stack frame instead of creating a new one for each recursive call.

Plus sur la récursion

Alors que les méthodes récursives sont intuitives et faciles à implémenter, elles peuvent parfois présenter des problèmes de performance en raison d'une utilisation excessive de la pile et d'une exécution plus lente. Une technique pour atténuer ces problèmes est la récursion terminale.

Récursion terminale

La récursion terminale est un type spécial de récursion où l'appel récursif est la dernière opération effectuée dans la fonction, c'est-à-dire qu'il n'y a pas d'opérations ou de calculs en attente après l'appel récursif. Cela permet au compilateur ou à l'interpréteur d'optimiser la récursion en réutilisant le cadre de pile actuel au lieu d'en créer un nouveau pour chaque appel récursif.

Recursion - Case Study (Statistics)

Binomial Coefficient | STATISTICS

Context

You are a Stats student who has come across a recursive definition of the Binomial Coefficient function i.e. n choose k, which is the number of ways to choose an unordered collection of k items from a collection of n items.

The formula is as follows:
C(n, k) = C(n − 1, k − 1) + C(n − 1, k), for all n and k such that 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1.

It is also important to note:

  • C(n, 0) = 1 [intuition: there is only 1 way to choose 0 items from a list of n]
  • C(n, n) = 1 [intuition: there is only 1 way to choose n items from a list of n].

You want to test this recursive definition using a recursive function.

Task

Write a recursive function that prints the binomial coefficient of two integers n and k, such that 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1. Your program should:

  1. For the cases mentioned above, return 1.
  2. Otherwise, if 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1 is not true, return 0.
  3. Otherwise, compute the binomial coefficient recursively and return the result.

Introduction

In this lesson, we will look over some insights of Software Objects and Classes.

Objects

Objects, in general, represent entities in the real-world. In programming, an object has a similar notion; they have their own space in the memory to save their information. For example, a player in a game can be an object which stores information relevant to it such as health points, color, skills, etc.

Example

Can you spot the objects in the following image? How many are there?


There are a total of 6 objects in the image above. Each of these image occupy some space and have their unique properties such as color and shape.

Classes

Loosely speaking, classes are a collection of objects who share some common attributes.

Example

Can you look for classes in the following image?


There are multiple ways of defining classes in this context. One may categorize objects above on basis of their shape. In this case, we will have 3 classes namely Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle. What attributes/properties can you assign to these classes? (Hint: What is uncommon between the circle objects?)

Another way of defining classes coulde be on the basis of their color. We may define classes as Red, Green, and Blue. Here, the shape could be an attribute. Another way could be of simply defining one class: GeometricObjects with attributes as shape and color. This will enclose all the objects in the image.

So how should we define our classes? Defining classes complelety depends on the sitation and in practice, one should choose whichever feels most natural.

Classes to Objects

In programming, we define classes to classify different objects. The process of creating an object from a given class (like a blueprint) is called instantiating the class and the created object is called an instance of the class.

Classes

In this lesson, we will learn about Object Oriented Programming which is a way of encapuslating complex structures in a more reusable format.

Before a deep dive, let us try to understand the notion of classes which holds as a blueprint for this complex structure. We take the example of polygon: a polygon is, loosely speaking, a closed geometric curve made out of line segments. Thus, in an abstract sense, our class will be polygon and the objects it can define could be a triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, etc.


In general, a class represents a blueprint of a group of objects of the same type.

A class has two major components: attributes (or instance variables) and methods (or actions).

  • Attributes are variables inside our class which define properties of the object. For example, in the class Polygon, number of sides could be an attribute.

  • Methods are functions inside our class which define actions that can be implimented on the object. For example, in the class Polygon, a function to find its perimeter could be an attribute.

Static Modifiers

Static Modifiers determine what attributes/methods truly depend on the objects. To access any static attribute/method, we do not need to instantiate the class. To access them, we can simply use the . operator on the class name itself. For example, Math.pow(3,4). They are created using the static keyword.
  • static attributes: Shared by all the instances (objects) of the class. Thus, if we change the value of a static attribute of an object, then the value of that attribute will change for all instances of that class. In practice, it is recommended to change the value of static attribute using the class name instead of changing it through object reference.
    • Example:
    public class Car { public static int year = 2023; // this is a static attribute }
  • static methods: Not tied to a specific object (they carry out a general function).
    • Example:
    public class Car { public static void avgSpeed() { // this is a static method System.out.println("Average speed of a car is 80mph"); } }

Modificateurs Statiques

Les modificateurs statiques déterminent quels attributs/méthodes dépendent véritablement des objets. Pour accéder à n'importe quel attribut/méthode statique, nous n'avons pas besoin d'instancier la classe. Pour y accéder, nous pouvons simplement utiliser l'opérateur . sur le nom de la classe lui-même. Par exemple, Math.pow(3,4).

Ils sont créés en utilisant le mot clé static.

  • Attributs statiques : Partagés par toutes les instances (objets) de la classe. Ainsi, si nous changeons la valeur d'un attribut statique d'un objet, la valeur de cet attribut changera pour toutes les instances de cette classe. En pratique, il est recommandé de changer la valeur de l'attribut statique en utilisant le nom de la classe plutôt que de le faire par référence à l'objet.
    • Exemple :
    public class Car { public static int year = 2023; // ceci est un attribut statique }
  • Méthodes statiques : Non liées à un objet spécifique (elles réalisent une fonction générale).
    • Exemple :
    public class Car { public static void avgSpeed() { // ceci est une méthode statique System.out.println("Average speed of a car is 80mph"); } }

Introduction

In this module, we will delve into the concept of inheritance, a powerful mechanism that establishes connections between classes. Just as we inherit certain traits from our parents in real life, in programming, classes are organized in a hierarchical structure to facilitate the sharing of properties and functionalities. Inheritance is usually established when there is a strong is-a type relation between child and parent.

Example

Consider the classes Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle. What common property do they share? They are all shapes and thus, we can define another class Shape which will have all the common attributes in Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle and these classes will simply be child classes of the parent Shape class. This is depicted by the following hierarchical diagram.

Here, Shape class is called the super class (or parent class) of its descendents and Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle classes are called the sub class (or child class) of its parent.

Remark. In Java, a class can have only one parent class.

What gets inherited?

Loosely speaking, almost all the properties (attributes and methods) of the parent class are inherited to the child class and these properties can either be used or modified in the child class. Thus, we may say that inheritance supports the notion of writing less and managable code as changing the definition of a certain attribute in parent class can likely make changes in child classes as well.

More specifically, all non-private instance variables are inherited along with all non-private methods. If we want to inherit an attribute/method while keeping it private, we use protected visibility modifier.

Introduction

Dans ce module, nous explorerons le concept d'héritage, un mécanisme puissant qui établit des connexions entre les classes. Tout comme nous héritons de certains traits de nos parents dans la vie réelle, en programmation, les classes sont organisées dans une structure hiérarchique pour faciliter le partage de propriétés et de fonctionnalités. L'héritage est généralement établi lorsqu'il existe une relation de type est-un entre l'enfant et le parent.

Exemple

Considérons les classes Circle, Rectangle et Triangle. Quelle propriété commune partagent-elles ? Ce sont toutes des formes, et donc, nous pouvons définir une autre classe Shape qui aura tous les attributs communs de Circle, Rectangle et Triangle, ces classes étant simplement des classes enfant de la classe parent Shape. Cela est représenté par le diagramme hiérarchique suivant.

Ici, la classe Shape est appelée la classe super (ou classe parent) de ses descendants, et les classes Circle, Rectangle et Triangle sont appelées la classe sub (ou classe enfant) de leur parent.

Remarque. En Java, une classe ne peut avoir qu'une seule classe parente.

Ce qui est hérité ?

En termes généraux, presque toutes les propriétés (attributs et méthodes) de la classe parent sont héritées par la classe enfant, et ces propriétés peuvent être utilisées ou modifiées dans la classe enfant. Ainsi, nous pouvons dire que l'héritage supporte l'idée d'écrire moins de code tout en le rendant plus gérable, car changer la définition d'un attribut dans la classe parente peut probablement entraîner des changements dans les classes enfants également.

Plus précisément, toutes les variables d'instance non privées sont héritées ainsi que toutes les méthodes non privées. Si nous voulons hériter d'un attribut/méthode tout en le gardant private, nous utilisons le modificateur de visibilité protected.

    Basic Definitions

    • Probability distributions are mathematical functions that output the probability of a particular event occurring out of all possible events.
    • An event can be discrete or continuous. For an event to be discrete, it means that there are countable or finitely many outcomes. For example, the outcome of a die roll can be a whole number from 1-6, but cannot be 1.318, for instance. The number of people in an office, the outcome of a coin flip, yes/no, are all discrete values.
    • The Probability Mass Function (PMF) of a discrete probability distribution is the probability of an event happening. Eg: if a dice is rolled, the PMF of getting any number is 1/6
    • The Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a discrete probability distribution is the cumulative probability of all events up to and including a particular event. Eg: if a die is rolled, the probability of getting a 3 or below = CDF(3) = the sum of all individual PMFs from 1-3.
    • A Discrete Uniform Distribution is where all events in an interval are equally likely. The parameters a and b represent the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Eg: the probability of picking any card out of a deck of 52 is said to follow a uniform distribution with a=1 and b=52.
    • A Binomial Distribution models a situation where the same experiment is repeated n times, and each time the probability of the particular event occurring is p. Eg: the number of Heads out of 3 coin flips is said to follow a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.5 (head or tails).

    Formulas:
    - For a Uniform Distribution: PMF(X) = 1/(b-a), for all X between a and b (inclusive).
    - For a Binomial Distribution: PMF(X) = binomialCoefficient(n,k) * px * (1-p)n-x
    - CDF(X) of any discrete distribution is the sum of all PMF's from 0 to X.

Constructor Chaining

Constructor chaining in the context of inheritance refers to the process of calling a superclass constructor from a subclass constructor. When you create an object of a subclass, it contains the superclass part as well. To properly initialize both the subclass and superclass members, the subclass constructor needs to call the appropriate superclass constructor. This ensures that all members in the inheritance hierarchy are initialized correctly.

Example

Let's illustrate constructor chaining in Java using a class hierarchy consisting of a superclass called Shape and a subclass called Rectangle.

Chaine de Constructeur

La chaîne de constructeur dans le contexte de l'héritage fait référence au processus d'appel d'un constructeur de superclasse à partir d'un constructeur de sous-classe. Lorsque vous créez un objet d'une sous-classe, il contient également la partie superclasse. Pour initialiser correctement à la fois les membres de la sous-classe et de la superclasse, le constructeur de la sous-classe doit appeler le constructeur approprié de la superclasse. Cela garantit que tous les membres dans la hiérarchie d'héritage sont correctement initialisés.

Exemple

Illustrons la chaîne de constructeur en Java en utilisant une hiérarchie de classes composée d'une superclasse appelée Shape et d'une sous-classe appelée Rectangle.

Basic Definitions

  • Probability distributions are mathematical functions that output the probability of a particular event occurring out of all possible events.
  • An event can be discrete or continuous. For an event to be discrete, it means that there are countable or finitely many outcomes. For example, the outcome of a die roll can be a whole number from 1-6, but cannot be 1.318, for instance. The number of people in an office, the outcome of a coin flip, yes/no, are all discrete values.
  • The Probability Mass Function (PMF) of a discrete probability distribution is the probability of an event happening. Eg: if a dice is rolled, the PMF of getting any number is 1/6
  • The Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a discrete probability distribution is the cumulative probability of all events up to and including a particular event. Eg: if a die is rolled, the probability of getting a 3 or below = CDF(3) = the sum of all individual PMFs from 1-3.
  • A Discrete Uniform Distribution is where all events in an interval are equally likely. The parameters a and b represent the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Eg: the probability of picking any card out of a deck of 52 is said to follow a uniform distribution with a=1 and b=52.
  • A Binomial Distribution models a situation where the same experiment is repeated n times, and each time the probability of the particular event occurring is p. Eg: the number of Heads out of 3 coin flips is said to follow a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.5 (head or tails).

Formulas:
- For a Uniform Distribution: PMF(X) = 1/(b-a), for all X between a and b (inclusive).
- For a Binomial Distribution: PMF(X) = binomialCoefficient(n,k) * px * (1-p)n-x
- CDF(X) of any discrete distribution is the sum of all PMF's from 0 to X.

Projectile Class

Context

You are given a parent class called Projectile, which represents a projectile launched into the air. The Projectile class has one attribute: initialVelocity (or initial_velocity, which represents the projectile's initial velocity (in m/s). The class also has a method for calculating the time of flight of the projectile if it was shot/thrown straight up with the specified initial velocity. You want to create classes to model a cannonball and an arrow, which are special cases of a projectile.

  • For the cannonball, picture a cannon on top of a cliff at a height of H, shooting a cannon with velocity v0. The cannon is not angled (i.e. the launch angle is zero and we will ignore it in this case).
  • For the arrow, picture an archer shooting an arrow at an angle θ. The archer is at ground level and the projectile flies through the air, landing back on the ground (i.e our initial and final heights are 0, and we will ignore them in this case).

For simplicity, we are ignoring air resistance.

Task

Your task is to create two subclasses Cannonball and Arrow that represent different types of projectiles.

  • Both subclasses should inherit the attribute for initial velocity from the Projectile class.
  • Both subclasses should override the method for calculating time of flight according to the formulas given below.
  • Each subclass should have additional attributes and methods as described below:

Basic Definitions

  • Probability distributions are mathematical functions that output the probability of a particular event occurring out of all possible events.
  • An event can be discrete or continuous. For an event to be discrete, it means that there are countable or finitely many outcomes. For example, the outcome of a die roll can be a whole number from 1-6, but cannot be 1.318, for instance. The number of people in an office, the outcome of a coin flip, yes/no, are all discrete values.
  • The Probability Mass Function (PMF) of a discrete probability distribution is the probability of an event happening. Eg: if a dice is rolled, the PMF of getting any number is 1/6
  • The Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a discrete probability distribution is the cumulative probability of all events up to and including a particular event. Eg: if a die is rolled, the probability of getting a 3 or below = CDF(3) = the sum of all individual PMFs from 1-3.
  • A Discrete Uniform Distribution is where all events in an interval are equally likely. The parameters a and b represent the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Eg: the probability of picking any card out of a deck of 52 is said to follow a uniform distribution with a=1 and b=52.
  • A Binomial Distribution models a situation where the same experiment is repeated n times, and each time the probability of the particular event occurring is p. Eg: the number of Heads out of 3 coin flips is said to follow a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.5 (head or tails).

Formulas:
- For a Uniform Distribution: PMF(X) = 1/(b-a), for all X between a and b (inclusive).
- For a Binomial Distribution: PMF(X) = binomialCoefficient(n,k) * px * (1-p)n-x
- CDF(X) of any discrete distribution is the sum of all PMF's from 0 to X.

ProbabilityDistribution Class

Context

Being a Statistics student, you have learn about probability distributions. You want to write a program to model some basic probability distributions to gauge your understanding. For this exercise, you are given a parent class called ProbabilityDistribution, which has one attribute: parameters, which is an array of doubles/floats representing the parameters for the probability distribution. The class has methods for calculating the Probability Mass Function and Cumulative Distribution Function of an event X occurring. You want to create classes to model a Uniform Distribution and a Binomial Distribution.

For simplicity, we are considering only discrete probability distributions, and you can assume all events are integers.

Task

Your task is to create two subclasses UniformDistribution and BinomialDistribution that represent different types of probability distributions.

  • Both subclasses should inherit the attribute for parameters from the ProbabilityDistribution class.
    • The constructor for UniformDistribution should take arguments for a, minimum value and b, maximum value
    • The constructor for BinomialDistribution should take arguments for n, the number of experiments and p, probability of each event
  • Both subclasses should override the methods for calculating PMF and CDF according to the formulas given below.

You do not need to create the main method, it has already been provided and is only for demonstration.

Basic Definitions

  • Probability distributions are mathematical functions that output the probability of a particular event occurring out of all possible events.
  • An event can be discrete or continuous. For an event to be discrete, it means that there are countable or finitely many outcomes. For example, the outcome of a die roll can be a whole number from 1-6, but cannot be 1.318, for instance. The number of people in an office, the outcome of a coin flip, yes/no, are all discrete values.
  • The Probability Mass Function (PMF) of a discrete probability distribution is the probability of an event happening. Eg: if a dice is rolled, the PMF of getting any number is 1/6
  • The Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a discrete probability distribution is the cumulative probability of all events up to and including a particular event. Eg: if a die is rolled, the probability of getting a 3 or below = CDF(3) = the sum of all individual PMFs from 1-3.
  • A Discrete Uniform

stribution Function (CDF) of a discrete probability distribution is the cumulative probability of all events up to and including a particular event. Eg: if a die is rolled, the probability of getting a 3 or below = CDF(3) = the sum of all individual PMFs from 1-3.
  • A Discrete Uniform Distribution is where all events in an interval are equally likely. The parameters a and b represent the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Eg: the probability of picking any card out of a deck of 52 is said to follow a uniform distribution with a=1 and b=52.
  • A Binomial Distribution models a situation where the same experiment is repeated n times, and each time the probability of the particular event occurring is p. Eg: the number of Heads out of 3 coin flips is said to follow a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.5 (head or tails).

    • Formulas:
    - For a Uniform Distribution: PMF(X) = 1/(b-a), for all X between a and b (inclusive).
    - For a Binomial Distribution: PMF(X) = binomialCoefficient(n,k) * px * (1-p)n-x
    - CDF(X) of any discrete distribution is the sum of all PMF's from 0 to X.

Basic Definitions

  • Probability distributions are mathematical functions that output the probability of a particular event occurring out of all possible events.

For example, the outcome of a die roll can be a whole number from 1-6, but cannot be 1.318, for instance. The number of people in an office, the outcome of a coin flip, yes/no, are all discrete values.

  • A Binomial Distribution models a situation where the same experiment is repeated n times, and each time the probability of the particular event occurring is p. Eg: the number of Heads out of 3 coin flips is said to follow a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.5 (head or tails).

Formulas:
- For a Uniform Distribution: PMF(X) = 1/(b-a), for all X between a and b (inclusive).

In this section, we will explore nested selection statements, an essential concept in programming that allows us to handle complex decision-making by placing one if or if-else statement inside another. This provides a deeper level of control over the flow of the program, enabling us to address more intricate scenarios.

Key Points:

- A nested if is an if statement inside another if statement. This setup is crucial for handling complex conditions and scenarios in Java.

- Proper indentation is crucial for readability in nested structures. It distinguishes between different levels of nesting and makes the code more understandable.

- Each if must be paired with a corresponding else if all potential conditions should be addressed, ensuring comprehensive decision-making logic in your Java programs.

- Nested statements can be as deep as necessary, though deeper levels can complicate readability and maintenance. It's recommended to balance the depth of nesting with the need for clarity and maintainability in your code.

Introduction

Dans cette leçon, nous allons examiner le concept de gestion des exceptions. De nombreuses fois, lors du travail sur une base de code, nous rencontrons des erreurs qui doivent être corrigées soit par débogage, soit en gérant l'erreur de manière appropriée.

La gestion des exceptions permet à un programme de faire face à des situations exceptionnelles et de continuer son exécution normale. Une exception est un objet qui représente une erreur ou une condition empêchant l'exécution de se dérouler normalement. Lorsqu'une erreur est détectée, le flux normal du code s'arrête et cet objet d'exception est créé. Toutes les exceptions standard en Java sont des sous-classes de la classe Throwable.

Checked and Unchecked Exceptions

The built-in exceptions can be categorized as

  • Checked Exceptions: These exceptions are compile-time exception i.e., they are checked by the complier during complilation time. For the code to complie successfully, it is important to handle these exceptions in the code properly.
  • Unchecked Exceptions: These exceptions are run-time exceptions i.e., they may occur when the code is executing. This can happen due to issues like bad input, division by zero, etc. As the complier does not check for these exceptions, we do not need to handle them until really required.

Checked and Unchecked Exceptions

The built-in exceptions can be categorized as

  • Checked Exceptions: These exceptions are compile-time exception i.e., they are checked by the complier during complilation time. For the code to complie successfully, it is important to handle these exceptions in the code properly.
  • Unchecked Exceptions: These exceptions are run-time exceptions i.e., they may occur when the code is executing. This can happen due to issues like bad input, division by zero, etc. As the complier does not check for these exceptions, we do not need to handle them until really required.

Exceptions vérifiées et non vérifiées

Les exceptions intégrées peuvent être catégorisées comme suit :

  • Exceptions vérifiées : Ces exceptions sont des exceptions de compilation, c'est-à-dire qu'elles sont vérifiées par le compilateur lors de la compilation. Pour que le code compile avec succès, il est important de gérer correctement ces exceptions dans le code.
  • Exceptions non vérifiées : Ces exceptions sont des exceptions d'exécution, c'est-à-dire qu'elles peuvent se produire lorsque le code est en cours d'exécution. Cela peut se produire en raison de problèmes tels qu'une mauvaise entrée, une division par zéro, etc. Comme le compilateur ne vérifie pas ces exceptions, il n'est pas nécessaire de les gérer sauf si c'est vraiment requis.

Introduction

Dans ce module, nous plongerons dans le concept de Polymorphisme, ce qui signifie plusieurs formes.

Comme discuté dans les modules précédents, une classe définit un type. Pour un type donné, nous définissons son supertype comme le type de sa super classe et son subtype comme le type de sa sous-classe (s'il y en a une). Le polymorphisme traite de la référence à un type avec son supertype.

Exemple

Considérons les classes Circle, Rectangle et Triangle, toutes étendant Shape. Ainsi, nous pouvons dire que tous les cercles sont des formes, tous les rectangles sont des formes, et tous les triangles sont aussi des formes. En contexte de programmation, ceci est vrai en raison du chaînage de constructeurs comme discuté dans le module précédent. Pour instancier un Circle, nous instancions d'abord un Shape et donc, tout objet de type Circle est aussi de type Shape.

Cette notion peut être généralisée comme suit : Chaque type est également un type de son supertype (s'il y en a un). Notez que la réciproque n'est pas vraie. Toutes les formes ne sont pas des cercles.

Introduction

In this module, we will delve into the concept of Polymorphism, which means multiple forms.

As discussed in previous modules, a class defines a type. For a given type, we define its supertype as the type of its super class and subtype as the type of its subclass (if any). Polymorphism deals with referencing a type with its supertype.

Example

Consider the classes Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle all of which extends Shape. Thus, we can say that all circles are shapes, all rectangles are shapes, and all triangles are shapes as well. In context of programming, this holds true because of constructor chaining as discussed in previous module. To instantitate Circle, we first instantitate Shape and thus, any object of type Circle is also of type Shape.

Binding

Binding refers to the connection between a method call and a method's definition.

Static Binding

When the binding is known at compliation time, it is called as Static Binding. In case of methods overloading, the compiler finds a matching method according method signature at compilation time.

Dynamic Binding

As stated in Rule 3 of Polymorphism, when calling a method on a variable, the definion of that method in the actual type is considered. This definition of the method in the actual type is indeed the lastest override definition in the inheritance chain until the actual type. This definion is determined during runtime and the process is called Dynamic Binding.

More preciesely, Dynamic binding is used for overridden method and happens during the runtime. Here, Java tries to bind the method call to a method definition up a class-inheritance hierarchy.

Binding

La liaison fait référence à la connexion entre un appel de méthode et la définition de la méthode.

Liaison Statique

Lorsque la liaison est connue au moment de la compilation, elle est appelée liaison statique. Dans le cas du surcharge des méthodes, le compilateur trouve une méthode correspondante en fonction de la signature de la méthode au moment de la compilation.

Liaison Dynamique

Comme indiqué dans la Règle 3 du polymorphisme, lors de l'appel d'une méthode sur une variable, la définition de cette méthode dans le type réel est considérée. Cette définition de la méthode dans le type réel est la dernière définition de remplacement dans la chaîne d'héritage jusqu'au type réel. Cette définition est déterminée pendant l'exécution, et le processus est appelé liaison dynamique.

Plus précisément, la liaison dynamique est utilisée pour les méthodes remplacées et se produit pendant l'exécution. Ici, Java tente de lier l'appel de méthode à une définition de méthode dans la hiérarchie d'héritage de classes.

    Naming Conventions

    Names used for classes, functions, and variables are called identifiers. When naming your components, you must follow a few rules:

    • An identifier must contain only letters (A to Z or a to z), numbers (0 to 9), and underscore (_).
    • All identifiers must start with a letter or _.
    • A keyword cannot be used as an identifier. For example, you can not name your variable if.
    • An identifier can be of any length.
    • Python is case-sensitive. This means the identifier print() is not the same as Print() or PRINT().

Dans cette leçon, vous découvrirez variables, constantes et types de données. Mais avant cela, vous devez connaître quelques notions de base sur la manière dont les données sont stockées dans la mémoire de l'ordinateur.

Une mémoire d'ordinateur (RAM) consiste en une séquence d'emplacements de mémoire pour stocker des programmes et des données. Chaque emplacement dispose d'un adresse numérique unique qui commence à 0. Vous pouvez considérer la mémoire comme une commode où chaque tiroir représente un emplacement mémoire. Supposons maintenant que vous donniez un numéro unique à chaque tiroir pour indiquer son emplacement ; le premier tireur reçoit le numéro 0, le second le 1, et ainsi de suite. Une adresse mémoire dans ce cas serait le numéro que vous attribuez à chaque tiroir.

Pourquoi avons-nous besoin de mémoire informatique ? Comme indiqué ci-dessus, la mémoire de l'ordinateur stocke les programmes et les données. Lorsque vous démarrez un programme, le programme est d'abord chargé dans la mémoire avant son exécution. Cela améliore les performances d'exécution. Après le démarrage de l'exécution, le programme peut sauvegarder et restaurer les données de la mémoire.

Comment tout cela est-il lié aux variables ? Le programme doit identifier où les données sont stockées dans la mémoire. Cela peut être fait en utilisant des adresses mémoire. Un moyen plus simple consiste à étiqueter ces emplacements de mémoire et à utiliser ces étiquettes lors de l'accès aux données. Pensez à étiqueter les emplacements de mémoire comme mettre un autocollant sur un tiroir avec un nom, comme dans l'exemple ci-dessous. Lorsque vous faites référence à ce tiroir, vous pouvez dire tiroir #3 ou tiroir Adam . Une variable est un nom que vous donnez à un emplacement mémoire dans votre programme.

Remarque : dans certains cas, un compilateur d'optimisation peut stocker une variable dans une mémoire spéciale appelée registre. Cependant, cela dépasse le cadre de cette introduction leçon.

In this lesson, you will learn about variables, constants, and data types. But before we do that, you need to know a few basics about how data is stored in the computer's memory.

A computer's memory (RAM) consists of a sequence of memory locations for storing programs and data. Each location has a unique numeric address which starts from 0. You can think of memory as a chest of drawers where each drawer represents one memory location. Now assume you give a unique number to each drawer to indicate its location; the first drawer gets the number 0, the second gets 1, and so on. A memory address in this case would be the number you give to each drawer.

Why do we need computer memory? As indicated above, computer memory stores programs and data. When you start a program, the program is first loaded into the memory before it is executed. This improves the execution performance. After execution starts, the program can save and restore data from the memory.

How is this all related to variables? The program needs to identify where the data is stored in the memory. This can be done using memory addresses. An easier way is to label those memory locations and using these labels when accessing data. Think of labeling memory locations as putting a sticker on a drawer with a name, as in the example below. When referring to that drawer, you can either say drawer #3 or Adam's drawer. A variable is a name you give to a memory location in your program.

Note: in some cases, an optimizing compiler may store a variable in a special memory called a register. However, this is beyond the scope of this introductory lesson.

Declaring and Initializing Variables

Declaring a variable means informing the compiler that this variable will be used in the program. Initializing a variable means to store data in a variable for the first time. We use the assignment operator = to store data in variables. The general syntax is:

datatype variable_name = initial_value;

In Java, you must specify a type when declaring a variable, e.g. use int for integers. This allows the compiler to do type checking. Java is, therefore, classified as a statically-typed language. In the example below, the keyword int indicates that the variable is of integer type, which means it can only store integers (whole numbers).

Data Types

Now that we learned how variables are used as containers to hold data, let us discuss the types of data used in our programs.

Java has two groups of data types: Primitives and Objects. At this point, we will focus primarily on primitives, while objects will be discussed in details later.

Primitive Datatypes

A primitive datatype specifies the memory size of a variable and the valid range of values a variable can store. For example, by indicating that x is of the type int in the examples in the previous section, the compiler reserves 4 bytes of memory for x, and it will only allow storing integers (whole numbers) that are restricted to the range indicated in the table below.

Overall, there are eight primitive types in Java:

Category Datatype Example Size Possible Values
Whole Numbers byte byte x = 54; 1 byte -128 to 127

Comme vous pouvez le voir, la valeur de x à la fin était 7. Ne laissez pas cela vous confondre. Le = L'opérateur en programmation n'est pas le même que le signe égal mathématique. À la place, c'est une opération informatique qui attribue la valeur à droite au variables à gauche. La façon dont nous utilisons les variables dépend de l'endroit où elles se trouvent par rapport à l'opérateur = :

  • Si une variable est située à droite de =, nous l'avons remplacé par sa valeur actuelle.
  • Si une variable est située à gauche de f = , nous l'utilisons pour stocker la valeur du côté droit de = .

Dans la déclaration x = x + 2, la valeur du l'expression x + 2 à droite est calculée en premier avec la valeur existante de x, qui est 5, résultant en la valeur 7. Ce résultat est ensuite affecté à la même variable x, car elle se trouve maintenant à gauche, mettant à jour son valeur à 7.

Increment and Decrement Operators

Unlike other languages, Python does not have increment ++ or decrement -- operators. These operators are used to increment or decrement a variable by 1. If you want to do this in Python, you need to write x += 1 or x = x + 1 to increment a variable x by 1, and x -= 1 or x = x - 1 to decrement x by 1.

If you want to learn about these operators and how they are used, please switch the lesson configuration options to another language (e.g. Java).

The print() Function

This function prints data we put inside () to the screen (by default). The data could be one of the following:

  • A single item, e.g., string or number. For example, print("abc") displays abc on the screen.
  • An expression of which result is printed. For example, print(4 + 2) displays 6.

You can send multiple items separated by commas , to this function. For example, print("I have", 3, "books") displays I have 3 books.

The print function, by default, will move the cursor to the next line after it prints the data.

Customizing print Function

To change the default behaviour of the print function, you can use this general syntax:

print(data, sep=, end=, file=file, flush=flush)
  • sep: changes the default separator. Example: print("I have", 3, "books", sep='*') prints I have*3*books.
  • end: changes the default behavior of moving to a new line. Example: print("Hi", end="") does not move the cursor to the next line.

Introduction

For example, informing users whether they are adults based on their age. The algorithm could be something like this:

Read user's age.
IF age is at least 18, THEN display "Adult".

Context

You asked yourself, can I write my own calculator software? You decided to try! Because you are smart, you attempted to code a calculator which can handle multiple math operations.

Task

Write the program that:

  • Asks the user to input the math equation with exactly two operations as a string, e.g. "3+4*5".
  • Parse the equation and determine the order of operations. Remembere that *, / always come before +,- when evaluating equation.
  • Calculate and display the result.

Assumptions:

To simplify the problem, assume that the equation string will

  • only include single-digit, positive integers and two of the four operators +, -, *, and /.
  • not have negative numbers, floating-point numbers, other operators, spaces, or brackets.
  • always be valid in the form d$d$d where d is a digit and $ is an operator.

That means the input string will always have 5 characters (3 digits and 2 operators).

That is, your program should be able to handle all these equations:

  • "4+2*3"
  • "4/2-3"

However, your program should not handle any of these:

  • "-4*2+3", negatives are not allowed
  • "4 + 2 + 3", spaces are not allowed.
  • "4*(2+3)", brackets are not allowed.
  • "4*2.2+3", floating-point numbers are not allowed.

Like an if statement, the code inside the while loop will only run if the condition is true. However, after executing the code, the condition is checked again; if it is still true, the loop body is executed again, and so on. If the condition is false, the program continues to the next code block right after the loop body.

do-while Loops

A do-while is the same as a while statement, except that it runs the loop body first then tests the condition. This means the loop body will always run at least once, even if the condition if false.

Floating Point Accuracy

As you may know, computers use binary format (0's and 1's) to represent data. This of course includes numeric data. This representation works well for whole numbers. However, it sometimes fails to accurately represent fractions. For example, the following code is expected to print 1.2 in both statements, right? However, the actual output of the second statement is 1.2000000000000002.

C++ French Mathematics text Programming_Languages Spoken_Languages System.out.println(1.2); //output: 1.2 System.out.println(1.1 + 0.1); //output: 1.2000000000000002 print(1.2) # output: 1.2 print(1.1 + 0.1) # output: 1.2000000000000002 print(1.2) # production: 1.2 print(1.1 + 0.1) # production: 1.2000000000000002 System.out.println(1.2); //production: 1.2 System.out.println(1.1 + 0.1); //production: 1.2000000000000002 cout << (1.2) << endl; //output: 1.2 cout << (1.1 + 0.1) << endl; //output: 1.2000000000000002 cout << 1.2 << endl //production: 1.2 cout << 1.2+0.1 << endl //production: 1.2000000000000002 C++ French Mathematics code Spoken_Languages

Where does this inaccuracy come from? This brings us back to the way computers represent data in binary (0 and 1). Many decimal fractions are approximated when stored in computers. The value 0.1 is represented in binary using a very long sequence 0.000110011001100110... which must be approximated in order to store it in computer memory.

A nice analogy is when you (human) want to write the fraction 2/3 as a decimal number. You will have to write 0.66666666666.. which is infinitely long, and you

ted in binary using a very long sequence 0.000110011001100110... which must be approximated in order to store it in computer memory.

A nice analogy is when you (human) want to write the fraction 2/3 as a decimal number. You will have to write 0.66666666666.. which is infinitely long, and you can only approximate it to something like 0.66667. The computer does the same thing with decimal fractions.

Why is this important to know here? As seen in the code above, the result of 1.1 + 0.1 is not equal to 1.2. Knowing that now, you should NOT use floating-point values with equality checking in loop condition.

Qu'est-ce que la structure des données

Une structure de données est une collection d'éléments de données stockés dans la mémoire afin que ils peuvent être utilisés efficacement. Il existe plusieurs types de structures de données, toutes conçu pour organiser les données d'une manière qui sert un objectif spécifique. Exemples de types des structures de données comprennent des tableaux, des listes, des arbres, des tas, etc., chacun avec ses propres manière de stocker et de récupérer des données. Différentes applications et tâches ont différents besoins et limitations, et donc il faut utiliser la structure de données type qui correspond le mieux à ces besoins.

What is Data Structure

A data structure is a collection of data items stored in the memory so that they can be used effectively. There are several types of data structures, all designed to arrange data in a way that serves a specific purpose. Example types of data structures include arrays, lists, trees, heaps, etc, each with its own way of storing and retrieving data. Different applications and tasks have different needs and limitations, and hence one should use the data structure type that best fits these needs.

Array Basics

What is an Array?

An array is a collection of data items of the same type stored under one variable. For example, we can create an array called grades to store the grades of 100 students. All these values will be stored under a single name grades (as opposed to creating 100 separate variables to store them).

Array Basics

What is an Array?

An array is a collection of data items of the same type stored under one variable. For example, we can create an array called grades to store the grades of 100 students. All these values will be stored under a single name grades (as opposed to creating 100 separate variables to store them).

In Python, you can implement arrays either using lists or arrays module. A key difference is, lists allow to store items of different datatypes while arrays module does not allow that. datatype[] arrayName = new datatype[arraySize]

3) Utilisation de System.arraycopy()

System.arraycopy() est une méthode intégrée qui permet de copier des éléments de tableau. La syntaxe est :

System.arraycopy(src, srcPos, dest, destPos, length)

Où :

  • src est le tableau source
  • srcPos est le début place dans la source array
  • dest le tableau de destination
  • destPos est le position de départ dans la destination data
  • length est le nombre d'éléments de tableau à copier.

Pour utiliser cette méthode pour cloner un tableau existant, vous devez d'abord créer un tableau vide de même taille que celui existant. Ensuite, utilisez System.arraycopy(src, 0, dest, 0, src.length) pour copier tous les éléments d'un tableau source src au tableau de destination dest.

In Python, a list is one of four built-in datatypes used to store collections of data; the other three are: Tuple, Set, and Dictionary. This lesson focuses on lists.

  • Allow different data types: Lists can store items of same or different types.

What actually happens when you call a function?

When calling a function, the flow of control shifts from the calling statement to the called function. After the function is completed, the control is shifted back to the calling statement.

Que se passe-t-il réellement lorsque vous appelez une fonction ?

Lors de l'appel d'une fonction, le flux de contrôle passe de l'appelant instruction à la fonction appelée. Une fois la fonction terminée, la commande est ramené à l'instruction d'appel.

What actually happens when you call a method?

When calling a method, the flow of control shifts from the calling statement to the called method. After the method is completed, the control is shifted back to the calling statement.

Déclarations

  • Une instruction est une action de votre programme qui est exécutée par le l'ordinateur.
  • Chaque déclaration peut être terminé par un point-virgule ;. Cependant, ce n'est pas obligatoire en Python.
  • print("Bonjour, World!")
    • print() est une fonction qui affiche toutes les données que nous mettons à l'intérieur ().
    • Dans cet exemple, "Hello, World!" sont les données que nous voulons imprimer. D'autres types de données peuvent être imprimés, y compris des nombres, par ex. print(3), et expressions, par exemple. print(3+5) qui affiche 8, plus à ce sujet est discuté plus tard.

Statements

  • A statement is an action in your program that is executed by the computer.
  • Every statement may be terminated by a semi-colon ;. However, this is not required in Python.
  • print("Hello, World!")
    • print() is a function that displays any data we put inside ().
    • In this example, "Hello, World!" is the data we want to print. Other data types could be printed including numbers, e.g. print(3), and expressions, e.g. print(3+5) which displays 8, More about this is discussed later.

    Names used for classes, functions, and variables are called identifiers. When naming your components, you must follow a few rules:

    • An identifier must contain only letters (A to Z or a to z), numbers (0 to 9), and underscore (_).

    • A keyword cannot be used as an identifier. For example, you can not name your variable if.
    • An identifier can be of any length.
    • Python is case-sensitive. This means the identifier print() is not the same as Print() or PRINT().

Dans cette leçon, vous découvrirez variables, constantes et types de données. Mais avant cela, vous devez connaître quelques notions de base sur la manière dont les données sont stockées dans la mémoire de l'ordinateur.

Une mémoire d'ordinateur (RAM) consiste en une séquence d'emplacements de mémoire pour stocker des programmes et des données. Chaque emplacement dispose d'un adresse numérique unique qui commence à 0. Vous pouvez considérer la mémoire comme une commode où chaque tiroir représente un emplacement mémoire. Supposons maintenant que vous donniez un numéro unique à chaque tiroir pour indiquer son emplacement ; le premier tireur reçoit le numéro 0, le second le 1, et ainsi de suite. Une adresse mémoire dans ce cas serait le numéro que vous attribuez à chaque tiroir.

Pourquoi avons-nous besoin de mémoire informatique ? Comme indiqué ci-dessus, la mémoire de l'ordinateur stocke les programmes et les données. Lorsque vous démarrez un programme, le programme est d'abord chargé dans la mémoire avant son exécution. Cela améliore les performances d'exécution. Après le démarrage de l'exécution, le programme peut sauvegarder et restaurer les données de la mémoire.

Comment tout cela est-il lié aux variables ? Le programme doit identifier où les données sont stockées dans la mémoire. Cela peut être fait en utilisant des adresses mémoire. Un moyen plus simple consiste à étiqueter ces emplacements de mémoire et à utiliser ces étiquettes lors de l'accès aux données. Pensez à étiqueter les emplacements de mémoire comme mettre un autocollant sur un tiroir avec un nom, comme dans l'exemple ci-dessous. Lorsque vous faites référence à ce tiroir, vous pouvez dire tiroir #3 ou tiroir Adam . Une variable est un nom que vous donnez à un emplacement mémoire dans votre programme.

Remarque : dans certains cas, un compilateur d'optimisation peut stocker une variable dans une mémoire spéciale appelée registre. Cependant, cela dépasse le cadre de cette introduction leçon.
